22	
23	type statusCache struct {
24		mu       sync.Mutex
25		statuses map[string]git.Status
26	}

28	// WithStatusCache returns a context that memoizes Status results.
29	//
30	// Install it only across a window that neither writes tracked files nor stages
31	// anything — otherwise later callers observe a stale status. Staging counts:
32	// .git/index lives inside .git/, but the index feeds the status diff, so an
33	// index write invalidates a cached result just as a worktree write does. Entire
34	// performs no index writes today (no SetIndex calls; the git subcommands on the
35	// hook paths are all index-read-only), which is what makes turn start a valid
36	// window. A hook that runs after the agent has edited files is not.
37	func WithStatusCache(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
38		return context.WithValue(ctx, statusCacheKey{}, &statusCache{
39			statuses: make(map[string]git.Status),
40		})
41	}

44	// carries a cache from WithStatusCache and the same worktree was already read.
45	//
46	// The returned map is shared with other callers holding the same cached ctx, so
47	// callers must treat it as read-only.
48	func Status(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (git.Status, error) {
49		worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // callers add their own context
52		}

54		cache, ok := ctx.Value(statusCacheKey{}).(*statusCache)
55		if !ok {

57		}

59		// Key on the worktree root rather than the repository pointer: callers on
60		// the same hook path open the repository independently.
